subject: Error with Bivariate GP, User-defined Distribution

messages.author: f56d4c6b6451e734
messages.subject: Error with Bivariate GP, User-defined Distribution
parts:
Hello everyone,

I am working on a bivariate Gaussian Process (point process) model with a user-defined distribution. I am getting the following error when I try to subset the bivariate model to be every other item in the vector.

"Error in parse(text = x, keep.source = FALSE)[[1]] : subscript out of bounds"

I've tried a couple of different methods for extracting every other element. I've sent replication code to Perry and Chris, but happy to send it to anyone else who might be interested in taking look or might be able to help.

I've looked through other similar problems on this group and I might need to use a nimbleFunctionLists, but I'm not sure. I've tried quite a bit of debugging and I think all of the dimensions listed in the code are correct.

Thank you!

Best,
Claire

---
Some more details:
I have a bivariate GP based on a Kronecker product. I would like to extract every other element in this vector. I created a function called subs_gp() that I hoped would accomplish this. I also included the direct subsetting in the "nimbleCode", where wtilda_2 is the GP vector of length 2*n, and w2_int is the vector of indices that is every other number (2,4,6...2*n).

  for(h in 1:n_total){
    w_s2[h] <- wtilda_s[w2_ind[h]]
  }

The problem comes below when I try to add this to a linear regression (the code is below). When I run configureMCMC() with the list of monitors, I get the error referenced above.

  for(i in 1:n_total) {
    logmarks[i] ~ dnorm(mean = va_nonspatial[i] + w_s2[i], sd = lin_sig)
  }

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Error with Bivariate GP, User-defined Distribution
parts:
hi Claire,

Thanks for this report (and for the off-list reproducible example). It looks like this is a bug on our side. 

The problem comes in trying to create conjugate samplers for the elements of alpha and gamma, which involves (via a series fo deterministic expressions) wtilda_s.

If I add full indexing to wtilde_s (i.e., change the final "[ , 1]" to "[1:two_ntotal, 1]", things work on my end:

wtilda_s[1:two_ntotal] <- (knon_prod(expcov(dist_knotuof_nk[1:n_total,1:n_knot], phi=phi, sigma=1), Lambda[1:2,1:2])%*%inverse(knon_prod(expcov(distance_latt[1:n_knot, 1:n_knot], phi=phi, sigma=1), Lambda[1:2,1:2]))%*%W_knot[1:two_nknot])[1:two_ntotal,1]

There is an additional issue, which is that even with the change above, nimble doesn't detect that it could assign conjugate samplers for the alphas and gammas. I haven't tracked down why, but given that, if you want to reduce the time spent in configureMCMC, you might as well skip having nimble check for conjugate samplers by adding "useConjugacy = FALSE" as an additional argument to configureMCMC.

-chris

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Error with Bivariate GP, User-defined Distribution
parts:
Whoops, should have waited to respond, as my final comment about the additional issue of not detecting conjugacy was not correct. 

The alphas and gammas are also involved in the likelihood for 'one', so NIMBLE should not (and does not) detect conjugacy for the alphas and gammas. 

So the only issue is that you need to add the full indexing in defining wtilda_s, and on the nimble side, I have filed an issue for us to fix the issue that lack of full indexing causes an error.

-chris
